title: Operational Truths: Reliability Sprint & Experiment Diary (30d)
content:
Purpose / framing:
This is a 30-day sprint-style experiment diary and cross-functional kickoff note focused on validating a small set of operational truths about SLO-driven recovery and graceful-degradation behavior across hosted and dedicated serving paths. Goal is to run realistic probes, measure error-budget behavior, harden runbooks, and produce a prioritized, low-friction rollout plan for the next 90 days.

Why a diary instead of a playbook: this doc intentionally captures messy, iterative notes: sketches, failed probes, quick wins, and unresolved assumptions we want to surface to stakeholders. Treat as source-of-truth for the experiment sprint.

Who should read this: platform-engineering leads, SREs, serving-runtime engineers, product-hosted-api PMs, solutions-eng.

Top-level hypothesis (H0):
- When we apply a coordinated, SLO-aware fallback choreography (model variant downgrade + request shadowing + cache priming) we reduce error-budget burn by >= 40% during transient capacity pressure without increasing p95 latency on healthy requests by >10%.

Primary success metrics (measurement plan):
- Error budget burn rate (secondary: 7-day rolling) — success if burn rate reduced >=40% under synthetic pressure tests.
- p95 latency (customer-facing route) — baseline to compare; failure if >10% regression.
- Successful automatic fallback rate — percent of degraded requests that fell back to compatible variant and returned within SLO. Target >= 95%.
- Observability coverage — traces and spans instrumented for fallback decision paths (instrumentation health = 100% for targeted routes).

Minimum viable experiment (MVE):
1) Select 3 representative routes: short-text generation (low-latency), chat-completion (maintain context), and embeddings (CPU-heavy).
2) Implement a lightweight fallback policy in proxy layer that can: downgrade to quantized model variant, route to dedicated pool, or respond with cached prefix where safe.
3) Traffic shadowing: send 5% of traffic to canary policy for 7 days (non-disruptive) then flip to 20% pressure test.
4) Run 3 synthetic pressure windows (10m, 30m, 2h) simulating burst patterns observed in last 6 months.

Sprint timeline (30 days):
- Day 0 (kickoff): align stakeholders, assign owners, create experiment runbooks and Slack channel.
- Day 1–6: lightweight proxy policy prototype + instrumentation; unit tests + local sandboxes.
- Day 7–12: deploy shadowing pipeline (5% traffic), verify telemetry, smoke tests.
- Day 13–18: controlled pressure window #1 (10m) — collect baseline and measure fallbacks.
- Day 19–22: iterate on policy thresholds, tweak cache TTLs, improve metrics.
- Day 23–26: pressure window #2 (30m), then #3 (2h) on final days.
- Day 27–30: analysis, runbook edits, stakeholder demo, recommended rollouts.

Stakeholders and responsibilities (working roster):
- Platform-engineering (owner): Maya Patel — overall experiment lead, rollout decision authority.
- Serving-runtime: Diego Martinez — implement safe downgrade hooks and KV cache priming APIs.
- Observability: Liam O'Connor — ensure spans/traces/metrics for fallback decision tree; build dashboards.
- Product-hosted-api PM: Sofia Ruiz — route selection, customer-impact risk assessment, acceptance criteria.
- Solutions/Customer Success: Priya Kapoor — surface customer use-cases, identify enterprise contracts that must be excluded from aggressive fallbacks.
- SRE on-call liaison: [rotating] — validate runbooks, operational playbook test.

Runbook sketch (for oncall use during experiments):
- Detection: alert when fallback rate exceeds threshold OR p95 latency regresses by >10% for >5m.
- Triage steps: check fallback decision logs; identify if policy misclassification (wrong route) or service strain (GPU shortage).
- Immediate mitigation: reduce traffic shadowing percentage to 0%, disable auto-downgrade, switch to canned fallback response (graceful degrade message).
- Post-incident: capture timeline, extract traces for failed decisions, schedule follow-up fix.

Instrumentation & dashboards to build (priority order):
1) Fallback decision trace: single-pane view for each request showing decision branch.
2) Error-budget burn rate per-route + root-cause tags (model-cache, infra, policy).
3) Traffic shadowing health widget: % mirrored vs served, latencies.

Small experiments / quick wins to try ASAP:
- Prefix cache priming for top-10 prompt templates used by customers — expect hit-rate improvement with little infra change.
- Lower eager-quantize threshold for non-sensitive routes so downgrade cost savings happen earlier.
- Short-circuit embeddings: if input length < 32 tokens, use CPU-optimized path to reserve GPUs.

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: customer-visible fidelity regressions during downgrades. Mitigation: omit SLAs for enterprise-tagged customers and validate with A/B quality checks on held-out prompt sets.
- Risk: telemetry blind spots (decision logs missing). Mitigation: instrument at both proxy and model-serving layers; start with high verbosity then throttle.
- Risk: cascading fallbacks causing alternative pool saturation. Mitigation: throttle fallback rate with circuit-breaker and backpressure signals.

Open questions / decisions to make quickly:
- Which enterprise customers are allowed to opt-in to experimental fallback? (Priya to provide whitelist by Day 2).
- What is the acceptable fidelity delta for each route (how measured)? Product to define 1–3 prompt-specific quality gates.
- Should rollback be automated (error-budget-based) or manual for first 60 days? Recommend manual for safety, auto if telemetry proves stable.

Deliverables at sprint close:
- Experiment report with time-series and annotated incidents.
- Updated runbook (markdown) checked into /confluence and linked in this doc.
- Playbook PR: policy config defaults + canary parameters for rollout.
- Decision log with recommendation: (1) promote policy to 10% production if success, (2) run 90-day additional monitoring, (3) start migration plan for enterprise exclusions.

Notes to self / loose thoughts (messy):
- The term "operational truths" is intentionally provocative: we want to surface assumptions that need to be proven before broad rollout (e.g., "KV cache priming pays off more than model-quantization at 95th percentile").
- Consider an "observability boomerang" test: intentionally break instrumentation for 1h in staging and validate alerting catches the absence of decision logs. Good test of detection coverage.
- Build a tiny harness that can replay production-like traffic (hash-preserving) to staging so we can iterate without touching prod.

Next immediate actions (Day 0–1):
- Create experiment runbooks in repo and assign owners (Maya).
- Priya to deliver enterprise exclusion list.
- Diego to prototype downgrade hook with a kill-switch flag.
- Liam to sketch the fallback decision trace dashboard.
- Create Slack channel: #ops-experiments/operational-truths

Appendix: quick links and references:
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-OPS-7812 (experiment background)
- Jira epic: JIRA-RELIAB-321 (tracking tasks)
- Infra PR for proxy policy stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987

(End diary entry — keep appending notes here as experiment proceeds)
